chapters.title: Chapter 2: How Each Component Is Taxed

lessons.title: Perquisites: Company Car, Rent-Free Housing, ESOPs and Other Benefits

children.text: Siddharth, a regional sales head in Mumbai, is offered a choice: a company-leased sedan with a driver and fuel, or ₹70,000 a month more in salary to arrange all of that himself. The car costs his employer ₹8,40,000 a year. For tax, it is valued at just ₹1,20,000.

That gap is the whole story of perquisites. When your employer gives you a benefit instead of cash, the Income-tax Rules, 2026 decide what it is "worth" for tax, and that value is often far below its real cost. Sometimes it is far above what you would expect. This lesson shows you both.

body.text: A perquisite is taxed at its rule value, not its market value. The gap between the two is where structuring lives.

children.text: Perquisites are taxed as salary under Section 17 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 17(2) of the 1961 Act), and valued under Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 (Rule 3 of the 1962 Rules). Because they are valuation rules and not exemptions, they apply the same way in both tax regimes.

body.text: Some benefits, like a company car, domestic help and utilities, are taxed only for "specified employees": directors, people with a substantial shareholding, and employees whose cash salary is above ₹4,00,000 a year. In practice, that covers almost every mid-level salaried professional reading this.

children.text: Perk 1: The company car

body.caption: Car owned or hired by the employer, used for both official and personal purposes, tax year 2026-27
headers: Engine up to 1.6 litres or electric

children.text: Only official use
, with a log book and employer certificate: no taxable value.
Only personal use
: actual running costs and driver salary, plus 10% of the car's cost a year for wear and tear. This is far more expensive for tax.

body.title: Siddharth: car as cash salary vs car as perquisite (annual)

children.text: Siddharth's sedan has a 2.0 litre engine. The employer pays the ₹40,000 monthly lease, ₹10,000 of fuel and a ₹20,000 driver. As a perquisite: (₹7,000 + ₹3,000) × 12 = ₹1,20,000. As cash salary, he would be taxed on the full ₹8,40,000. The perquisite route keeps ₹7,20,000 out of his taxable salary, saving ₹2,24,640 at 31.2%.

body.text: The 2026 rules roughly tripled car perquisite values. The same car and driver were valued at ₹39,600 a year under the old rules. If your company car was set up years ago, expect higher TDS from April 2026 even though nothing about the car changed.

children.text: Perk 2: Rent-free or company-leased housing

Transferred employees, bank officers and senior managers often get housing instead of HRA. Its taxable value is not the market rent, but a percentage of salary based on the city's population as per the 2011 census.

body.latex: \text{Accommodation perquisite} = (\%\ \text{of salary}) + 10\% \times \text{Furniture cost} - \text{Rent recovered from you}
body.caption: For employer-leased housing, the % of salary figure is replaced by the lower of the actual lease rent and 10% of salary.

cells: Mysuru, Dehradun, Guwahati and smaller cities
Lower of actual charges and 24% of salary

body.text: "Salary" for housing includes basic, taxable allowances, bonus and commission, but excludes DA not counted for retirement benefits, employer PF, exempt allowances, perquisites and gratuity. So it is wider than the salary used for HRA.

children.text: Anjali, a banker transferred to Bengaluru, lives in a company-leased flat with a market rent of ₹60,000 a month. Her salary for this purpose is ₹24,00,000, and she pays her employer ₹5,000 a month towards rent.

stats.label: 10% of salary
stats.context: Lower than lease rent, so this applies

children.text: If the flat also came with ₹5,00,000 of furniture owned by the employer, another 10% of that cost (₹50,000) would be added, taking the perquisite to ₹2,30,000.

body.title: Vivek in Mysuru
body.prompt: Vivek works at a manufacturing plant in Mysuru and lives in an unfurnished house owned by his employer. His salary for this purpose is ₹9,60,000 and he pays no rent. What is the taxable value of the accommodation?
body.explanation: Mysuru's population is below 15 lakh, so the value is 5% of salary: 5% × ₹9,60,000 = ₹48,000. Nothing is recovered from him, so the full ₹48,000 is added to his taxable salary.

children.text: Perk 3: Interest-free and cheap loans

If your employer lends you money at below-market interest, the benefit is taxed. The value is interest at State Bank of India's rate for a similar loan on 1 April of the tax year, minus the interest you actually pay. Two carve-outs: loans for treatment of specified diseases, and small loans where your total borrowing from the employer does not exceed ₹2,00,000, up from ₹20,000.

body.title: Just over the line
body.question: Neha takes a ₹2,50,000 interest-free loan from her employer for her wedding, outstanding all year. Assume SBI's rate for a similar personal loan on 1 April was 11%. What is the taxable perquisite?
body.explanation: The ₹2,00,000 relief applies only when the total loan does not exceed ₹2,00,000. It is not a deduction from a bigger loan. Once Neha borrows ₹2,50,000, interest on the entire amount is valued: 11% × ₹2,50,000 = ₹27,500. Keeping the loan at ₹2,00,000 would have made it fully tax-free.

children.text: Perk 4: ESOPs and RSUs

Stock options are taxed twice: once as a perquisite when you exercise, and again as capital gains when you sell. The first charge is where people get caught out, because you owe tax on shares you have not sold.

events.title: Options are granted
events.description: No tax. You have a right, not shares.

events.title: Options vest
events.description: No tax yet. You can now exercise.

events.title: You pay the exercise price and receive shares
events.description: Taxed as salary: (fair market value on exercise date minus exercise price) × shares. Your employer deducts TDS under Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025.

events.title: You sell the shares
events.description: Capital gains on sale price minus the fair market value used at exercise. For listed shares held over 12 months, long-term gains above ₹1,25,000 a year are taxed at 12.5%.

body.latex: \text{ESOP perquisite} = (\text{FMV on exercise date} - \text{Exercise price}) \times \text{Number of shares}
body.caption: Listed shares: FMV is the average of the opening and closing price on the exercise date. Unlisted shares: value set by a merchant banker.

children.text: Rohan works at a Nifty 50 listed IT company. He exercises 500 options at an exercise price of ₹400. On that day the stock opens at ₹1,480 and closes at ₹1,520.
Perquisite = (₹1,500 − ₹400) × 500 = ₹5,50,000, added to his salary
At 31.2%, tax on exercise = ₹1,71,600, collected through TDS, even though he has sold nothing

body.title: Show the working: Rohan sells 14 months later at ₹1,800

children.text: Cost for capital gains is the FMV at exercise, not the ₹400 he paid: ₹1,500 × 500 = ₹7,50,000
Long-term capital gain: ₹1,50,000
Less the ₹1,25,000 annual exemption for listed equity (assuming no other such gains): ₹25,000 taxable
Using ₹400 as cost would double-count the ₹5,50,000 already taxed as salary. Always check that your broker or tax software uses FMV at exercise as your cost.

body.title: Kavya's exercise
body.prompt: Kavya exercises 120 options in her listed employer at an exercise price of ₹600. On the exercise date the stock opens at ₹2,150 and closes at ₹2,250. What is the taxable perquisite?

body.text: Work at an eligible start-up? If it is DPIIT-recognised and certified under Section 140 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 80-IAC of the 1961 Act), tax on the ESOP perquisite can be deferred until you sell, leave the company, or a fixed period ends, whichever is first. For shares allotted from 1 April 2026 that period is 60 months from the end of the tax year of allotment. Our ESOPs course covers this in depth.

body.title: The small loan rule
body.textWithBlank: Interest-free loans from your employer are not taxed if the total amount of such loans does not exceed ₹___.
body.explanation: The Income-tax Rules, 2026 raised this limit from ₹20,000 to ₹2,00,000. Above it, interest on the entire loan is valued at SBI's rate, unless the loan is for treatment of a specified disease.

body.title: HRA or company flat?
body.scenario: Anjali's employer offers her a choice for her Bengaluru posting: HRA of ₹60,000 a month to rent a flat herself, or a company-leased flat with the same ₹60,000 market rent, where she pays ₹5,000 a month and the rest of her salary is unchanged. Her salary for perquisite purposes is ₹24,00,000. She is in the new tax regime and in the 30% slab.
body.prompt: Which option leaves Anjali with more money after tax, and by roughly how much? Is there any reason she might still prefer HRA?
body.modelAnswer: With HRA in the new regime, the full ₹7,20,000 is taxable, costing ₹2,24,640 in tax at 31.2%, and she pays ₹7,20,000 of rent herself. With the company flat, her taxable perquisite is only ₹1,80,000, costing ₹56,160 in tax, and she pays her employer ₹60,000 a year. Assuming her employer cuts her HRA to nil but keeps everything else the same, compare what she keeps. HRA route: receives ₹7,20,000, pays ₹7,20,000 rent and ₹2,24,640 tax on it, so she is ₹2,24,640 worse off. Company flat: pays ₹60,000 recovery and ₹56,160 tax, so she is ₹1,16,160 worse off. The company flat is better by about ₹1,08,000 a year. She might still prefer HRA if she wants to choose her own location or flat, plans to switch jobs soon and would lose the flat, or if she moves to the old regime and her HRA exemption becomes large. The flat also ties her housing to her employment.

body.text: Values are based on Section 17 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 for tax year 2026-27. Perquisite rules have further conditions, and SBI rates and share prices used here are assumptions for illustration. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax advice.

points: Perquisites are valued by Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, and the same values apply in both tax regimes.
A company car used for both work and personal trips is valued at ₹5,000 or ₹7,000 a month plus ₹3,000 for a driver, far below its real cost but about triple the old values.
Company housing is valued at 10%, 7.5% or 5% of salary depending on city population, often far below market rent.
Interest-free loans are tax-free only if total loans stay within ₹2,00,000.
ESOPs are taxed as salary on exercise, on FMV minus exercise price, and again as capital gains on sale, using FMV at exercise as cost.
Laptops, meals up to ₹200, gifts up to ₹15,000 and group health cover carry no or limited tax value.
